name: SkillSpector
description: Security scanner for AI agent skills. Detect vulnerabilities, malicious patterns, security risks, prompt injection, data exfiltration, and supply-chain risks in Claude Code, Codex, and MCP skills before you install them.
one_liner: A security scanner that checks whether an AI agent 'skill' (an add-on for tools like Claude Code) is safe to install, or secretly malicious.
buyer: A security or platform engineering lead at a company that lets employees install third-party AI agent skills and worries about supply-chain attacks.
business_use_cases: An enterprise security team wires it into CI so no AI agent skill gets installed company-wide without passing a scan.
A marketplace for AI skills (like a plugin store) runs it automatically on every submission before listing.
A security consultancy offers 'AI supply-chain audits' for companies rolling out agentic coding tools, using it as the core scanner.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a hosted scanning-as-a-service API that skill marketplaces or enterprises pay to call per scan.
Sell an enterprise dashboard/reporting layer on top of the open-source scanner for compliance teams.

steal_this: Scan every skill in a popular public skill marketplace this weekend, publish the vulnerability stats as a report, and use it to pitch a paid monitoring subscription to that marketplace.
